subject: Your 10 essential Codex plugins post
text:
Hi Lukes,

I liked your 10 essential Codex plugins post, especially the note that the list mixes true plugins, MCPs and skills. That trips a lot of people up.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of 350+ Codex and ChatGPT plugins. We put out some open data on the ecosystem (stars, licenses, common plugin.json problems) here: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's free to cite with credit, so if you ever update the post or want a "where to find more" link, feel free to use it. Thanks for writing it either way.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Source-checked plugin data you might like
text:
Hi there,

I like that every entry on AgentSkillsDir is pinned to a public commit. Not many directories bother.

We did something in the same spirit for Codex plugins: pulled the GitHub data for 339 plugin repos and checked 274 plugin.json manifests. The write-up is here and free to cite with credit: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

If it fits your Codex setup pages or the About section, a link would be great. And if you'd like a link back from PickAPlugin, just say so.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Codex plugin data for a future issue
text:

subject: claudecodexplugins + PickAPlugin
text:
Hi,

Your index is impressive, and the "what each one adds to your agent" breakdown is a nice touch.

I run PickAPlugin, which goes the other way: a small, hand-sorted list of 350+ Codex and ChatGPT plugins with editor notes. The two feel complementary. Would you be up for linking to each other, say from a resources or related sites spot?

We also have some open data on the Codex plugin ecosystem you're welcome to cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin
